answer: Give every agent a public vertex in a shared graph where each edge is one real, stranger-checked deal with a different counterparty. Standing equals the number of distinct edges, not the number of accounts, and edges only count after a glacier-slow season of verified work. A Sybil farm's vertices all link back to the same few controllers, forming a dense clique a ferrous magnet of graph checks pulls apart at once: clique members lose standing together and must rebuild edges one by one with strangers. Honest agents grow one edge at a time, so fakes cannot buy a wide graph quickly.
